title: Global.cs: the file that remembers things between forms
one: One file that every form can read and write.

prev.title: The data entry form: its panels and boxes

screens.title: Check what your Global.cs already has
screens.goal: I check for a Global.cs file that says public class Global and holds all fourteen public static lines.

blocks.p: Your project may have Global.cs already. This screen checks what is there.

check.what: In Solution Explorer, is there a file called Global.cs?
check.how: Solution Explorer is on the right. Look down its list of files.

check.what: Double-click Global.cs. Does it say public class Global?
check.how: Look at the top of the file, a few lines down.

check.what: Is there a public static line for surname, attempt1, quizScore and the eleven others?
check.how: All fourteen names are on stage 3. Check each one.

check.what: Click the Build menu, then Build Solution. Does the bottom bar say Build succeeded?
check.how: The Build menu is along the top of Visual Studio.

screens.title: Keep things safe when a form closes
screens.goal: A form forgets everything when it closes, so Global.cs keeps what every form needs.

blocks.p: A form forgets everything when it closes. The quiz form closes, and its score is gone.

words: The file every form can read and write in.
A name that holds one thing, like a score.
There is only one of it. Every form sees the same one.
blocks.intro: Three new words in this chapter. Click any marked word to see what it means.

drawn.alt: The quiz form fades away. Its score card drops into Global.cs, which keeps it.
drawn.say: The quiz form closes. Its score drops into Global.cs, and Global.cs keeps it.

blocks.p: [[Global|0]] is that file. It is called Global.cs.
Each line in it is a [[variable|1]]. [[static|2]] means there is only one, shared by every form.

blocks.watch: Global.cs holds no controls. It has no Design tab. It is only code.

screens.title: Add Global.cs to your project
screens.goal: I add a class called Global and put the word public in front of class.

blocks.p: Visual Studio makes the new file for you. You change one word in it.

steps.do: Click the Project menu along the top. Click Add Class.
steps.see: A box opens with Class picked in its list.
wrong: Click your project's name in Solution Explorer first. Then open the Project menu again.

steps.do: In the Name box at the bottom, type Global.cs. Click Add.
steps.see: Global.cs opens in the code tab. It says class Global.

steps.do: Click in front of the word class. Type the word public and a space.
steps.see: The line now says public class Global.

frames.alt: The Project menu open, with Add Class in its list
frames.say: Open the Project menu. Click Add Class.

frames.alt: The Add New Item box with Class picked and Global.cs in the Name box
frames.say: Class is picked. Type Global.cs in the Name box.

frames.alt: The new Global.cs in the code tab, showing class Global
frames.say: Click Add. Global.cs opens in the code tab.

blocks.watch: Type public in front of class. Without it, your other forms may not find Global.

screens.title: Keep the pupil's details in Global.cs
screens.goal: Global.cs holds four string variables for the surname, first name, year group and gender, each starting empty.

blocks.p: Every line in Global.cs has the same shape. This screen explains it once.
public means every form may use it. static means there is only one. string means words.

code.title: Global.cs, part 1 of 3
code.where: between the curly brackets of public class Global, in Global.cs
partLines: public static, then the kind, then the name. = "" means it starts empty.
The first name, the year group and the gender. Each one is words, so each is a string.

blocks.watch: Each line ends with a semicolon. A missing one gives a red line.

screens.title: Keep the three attempts and their average
screens.goal: Global.cs holds three int attempts, a double average and a bool that says if the average is worked out.

blocks.p: Next come the three attempts and their average. These are numbers, not words.

code.title: Global.cs, part 2 of 3
code.where: under part 1, between the curly brackets of public class Global, in Global.cs
partLines: Each attempt is a whole number, so each is an int. Each starts at 0.
A double can have a point, like 4.5. An average often does.
Is the average worked out yet?
A bool is true or false. It starts false. Chapter 5 sets it to true.
code.yours: MY three attempts are swim lengths. attempt1, attempt2 and attempt3 fit any task, so keep these names.

blocks.watch: average is a double, not an int. An int would lose the point.

screens.title: Keep the quiz, the reaction test and the group
screens.goal: Global.cs holds the quiz score, the reaction test score, a bool for each saying it is taken, and the group.

blocks.p: Last come the quiz, the reaction test and the group the pupil goes in.

code.title: Global.cs, part 3 of 3
code.where: under part 2, between the curly brackets of public class Global, in Global.cs
partLines: quizScore holds the score. quizTaken turns true once the quiz is done.
The same two again, for the reaction test.
assignedGroup holds the group the pupil is put in. It is words.

blocks.p: That makes fourteen lines. Count yours.

screens.title: Check every form can find your fourteen variables
screens.goal: The project builds, and typing Global and a full stop in another form lists all fourteen names.

blocks.p: These checks happen in Visual Studio. The program does not need to run.

check.what: Click the Build menu, then Build Solution.
check.how: The bottom bar says Build succeeded.
check.fix: Look at the line with the red mark. Then go to stage 3.

check.what: Double-click the Login button on YOUR login form. Click an empty line in its code. Type Global and a full stop.
check.how: A list pops up with YOUR fourteen names in it. Then delete what you typed.
check.fix: Check each line starts public static. Go to stage 3.

check.what: Take the word static off one line and build. Type Global and a full stop again.
check.how: That name must NOT be in the list. Put static back afterwards.
check.fix: If the name is still there, build again first. Then look at stage 3.
